---
title: "4i / Cyclic IF"
---

Cyclic immunofluorescence images the same plate several times, stripping and
re-staining between rounds. Instead of the three or four markers a single round
allows, you measure dozens per cell — provided the rounds can be registered
accurately enough to say that a nucleus in round 3 is the *same* nucleus as in
round 1.

That registration problem is what this part of OMERO-Screen solves.

## The idea

Each round is analysed as an ordinary plate: segmented, measured, stored. The
4i tools then run afterwards, computing a geometric alignment between rounds,
matching cells across them, and merging the per-round features into one
single-cell table.

Nothing about the per-round analysis is special. If you can run a plate, you
can run a 4i experiment.

## The workflow

| Step | Tool | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `omero-screen` | Analyse **each round** as a normal plate |
| 2 | [`align_plates.py`](alignment.qmd) | Register the rounds against a reference |
| 3 | [`create_masks.py`](alignment.qmd#filling-in-missing-masks) | Fill in cell masks missing from secondary rounds |
| 4 | [`aggregate_plates.py`](aggregation.qmd) | Merge per-cell features across rounds |
| 5 | [`alignment_qc.py`](quality-control.qmd) | Check the registration actually worked |

The first plate passed to `align_plates.py` is the **reference**. Every other
round is registered onto it, and the aggregated dataset carries its plate ID.

## Before you start

::: {.callout-warning}
These are `bin/` utilities and still use argparse, unlike the four main
commands. They keep argparse conventions — including abbreviated options — and
are run with `python bin/<name>.py` rather than as installed commands.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
`--sample-alignments` must be set **consistently** across steps 2, 3 and 4.
Mixing per-sample and per-well alignments produces silently wrong mappings —
no error, just cells matched to the wrong partners.
:::

## Analysing the rounds

Run the pipeline on each round separately, exactly as for a single-round
experiment:

```bash
uv run omero-screen 4126 --stitch
uv run omero-screen 4127 --stitch
uv run omero-screen 4128 --stitch
```

Each round gets its own segmentation, features and QC. At this point nothing
knows the rounds are related — that begins with
[alignment](alignment.qmd).
